fixes.explanation: David says, “You have tested me and found no evil…” (Psalm 17:3) He's saying the LORD tried his heart and even visited him in the night. I think David is laying his whole heart out where God can see it.
David talks about a tested heart, but he doesn't say God found doubt there. What he says is, “You have tested me and found no evil…” (Psalm 17:3) That's the report David gives.

Forgiveness is a big and wonderful thing, friend, but it showed up at the wrong verse. David says, “I call on You, O God, for You will answer me.” (Psalm 17:6) Forgive is a fine word, it just didn't get the job here. The word he uses is answer.
David says God saves by His right hand “…those who seek refuge from their foes.” (Psalm 17:7) The people he names are the ones who seek refuge. The trouble they're seeking refuge from is their foes.

Not one offering shows up in this verse, friend. David says God saves by His right hand “…those who seek refuge from their foes.” (Psalm 17:7) The people he names are the ones seeking refuge, and that's the whole list.

Priests? I looked through this whole prayer, friend, and there's not one in it. David asks to be hidden “…from the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.” (Psalm 17:8-9) Those are the ones he names.

Crowds didn't make the guest list in this prayer, friend. David asks to be hidden “…from the wicked who assail me, from my mortal enemies who surround me.” (Psalm 17:8-9) The ones he names are the wicked and the mortal enemies.

A wolf makes a fine villain, but it's not the one David picks. He says, “…like a lion greedy for prey, like a young lion lurking in ambush.” (Psalm 17:12) The animal is a lion, and he says it twice, a lion and then a young lion.

Nice thought, friend, but there are no peace talks in this verse. David prays, “Arise, O LORD, confront them! Bring them to their knees…” (Psalm 17:13) He asks God to confront them and bring them down.

Battles is a tempting guess with that lion in the psalm, but David doesn't pray for them to be left behind. He says, “…so they leave their abundance to their children.” (Psalm 17:14) What's handed down is abundance.
Silent isn't the word David uses, friend. He says, “when I awake, I will be satisfied in Your presence.” (Psalm 17:15) He ends on satisfied.
